title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The policy proposes creating an Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the President’s Executive Office to monitor and address risks from AI and other advanced technologies. It also establishes additional responsibilities and authorities for this office to coordinate national efforts in managing emerging tech threats.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 is a law designed to boost the development of safe, trustworthy AI by establishing clear standards and best practices for researchers and developers. It also creates funding opportunities, oversight mechanisms, and collaborative frameworks to ensure that new AI systems are transparent, reliable, and aligned with societal values.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a federal task force dedicated to protecting AI systems and infrastructure from cyber threats. It aims to coordinate security best practices, share threat intelligence, and develop policies to safeguard AI technology across critical sectors.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Act establishes a framework for identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks associated with artificial intelligence, requiring organizations to implement comprehensive risk‑management protocols. It also sets security standards and reporting obligations to protect AI systems from vulnerabilities, misuse, and potential harm.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 creates a new government board that will investigate cybersecurity incidents involving artificial intelligence. The act sets up rules and procedures for how the board will operate, who it can investigate, and what actions it can take.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: The resolution creates a Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to oversee the development and use of AI technology. The committee will study AI’s impacts, recommend policy measures, and provide oversight to ensure responsible use of AI.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is a law that bars artificial intelligence from performing any tasks that a human doctor would normally do. It is designed to keep medical care strictly in the hands of licensed physicians and prevent AI from diagnosing, prescribing, or providing treatment to patients.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 aims to assess and mitigate potential risks associated with AI technologies. It establishes guidelines for evaluating AI systems’ safety and ethical impact before deployment.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed legislative framework that aims to regulate the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence systems to ensure safety, transparency, and accountability. It outlines requirements for risk assessments, data governance, and oversight mechanisms, while also promoting responsible innovation and protecting citizens' rights.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act is a proposed law that would pause the construction of new data centers designed for AI operations. It seeks to address concerns about environmental impact, energy use, and the concentration of AI infrastructure, giving regulators time to develop guidelines before new facilities can be built.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is a proposed law that seeks to regulate and reduce the environmental footprint of AI technologies by requiring companies to conduct impact assessments and report on energy consumption, carbon emissions, and waste generation. It also establishes guidelines for more sustainable AI development, encourages the use of renewable energy sources, and sets penalties for non-compliance to promote greener AI practices.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act aims to ensure artificial intelligence technologies are developed and used in ways that benefit U.S. citizens and strengthen the economy. It calls for federal oversight, investment in AI research, and safeguards to protect privacy and public safety.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a proposed law that seeks to give students and teachers the knowledge and skills needed to understand and responsibly use artificial intelligence. It would establish standards for AI education, fund teacher training and classroom resources, and work to ensure every student has access to AI learning opportunities.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 seeks to establish standards and oversight for AI research to ensure safety, transparency, and reliability. It aims to promote responsible development through funding, regulation, and accountability measures for AI projects.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to set up a pilot program that employs AI to strengthen cyber defense for critical infrastructure. It also outlines additional measures and purposes related to the program’s implementation and oversight.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a federal law that aims to prepare students and educators for the growing influence of artificial intelligence by establishing comprehensive AI literacy programs across schools. It requires schools to incorporate AI education into curricula, provides teacher training and resources, and sets standards for AI readiness to ensure students can safely and effectively use AI tools.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: This act establishes guidelines and accountability measures for using AI in processing Veterans Affairs claims. It aims to ensure transparency, fairness, and oversight to protect veterans' rights when automated systems determine claim outcomes.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 is a law aimed at making the use of artificial‑intelligence systems by Virginia state agencies open and understandable to the public. It requires agencies to disclose when they employ AI, explain how those systems work and the data they rely on, and to conduct regular impact assessments so citizens can see how AI decisions affect their lives.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act is designed to launch a nationwide effort that informs citizens about the benefits, risks, and responsible use of artificial intelligence. It establishes funding and partnerships among federal agencies, schools, and industry to develop educational materials, public outreach programs, and curriculum standards that increase understanding of AI technologies.

title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: The Senate has passed a resolution stressing the need to protect religious freedom as artificial intelligence becomes more pervasive, urging that people be able to practice their faith without interference from AI systems. It also calls for AI technologies to be designed with clear transparency and guided by trustworthy sources or authoritative texts to ensure accountability and public trust.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: This act is designed to protect consumers from deceptive AI practices by setting clear standards for transparency and accountability. It requires companies to disclose when AI is used and imposes penalties for misleading or deceptive AI content.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy requires the Director of National Intelligence to give Congress a report on how artificial intelligence is used to gather, analyze, query, share, or otherwise handle information under the surveillance authority granted by section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. It aims to ensure Congress is kept informed about AI’s role in foreign intelligence activities.

title: Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026 seeks to modernize educational programs so students acquire AI skills from an early age and to develop national training initiatives that prepare workers for AI‑driven careers. By integrating AI literacy into K‑12 curricula and providing scholarships, workforce certifications, and industry partnerships, the Act aims to close the skills gap and boost economic competitiveness.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 26 - 21.
summary: The Open‑Source AI Leadership Act is designed to encourage the creation and use of open‑source AI technologies by establishing guidelines that promote transparency, collaboration, and shared stewardship. It seeks to give incentives and support to developers and organizations that lead open‑source AI projects, ensuring that these innovations are accessible, ethically guided, and widely beneficial.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 is a proposed law to curb companies from overcharging for AI services and manipulating wages for AI‑related workers. It would establish rules that enforce fair pricing and protect labor rights within the rapidly expanding AI industry.
